correctness.rationale: Exact Q(sqrt5) arithmetic constructs 12 icosahedron vertices, 20 facet normals, the 30-edge original and dual graphs; proves no three great circles concurrent in either arrangement; exhaustively enumerates 32 and 92 chambers from pairwise intersections and their four local sectors. For every one of the 20 T=12 triangular sign cones, all three extreme rays satisfy a single shadow S=6 cone sign mask, proving containment for all generic normals. Exact angle signatures plus Girard spherical excess give every probability; independent edge-separation Crofton formulas check the means and covariance. Standalone verify.py was executed successfully; no finite sampling used as proof. Four exact generic integer-coordinate witnesses also establish strictly positive open sets for all four supported pairs.

originality.rationale: Only the same-normal joint refinement and strict implication T=12 implies S=6 are proposed. The icosahedron section marginal is a published prior result; the icosahedron shadow marginal is known through the polar dodecahedron section law. General random-shadow bounds and section count studies do not imply the joint law. Ten actual semantic source searches, close published-finding corpus records and inspected primary texts support provisional originality, with explicit residual priority risks.
residual_risks: Unindexed old stereological or visualization calculation could contain the joint same-normal normal-fan refinement; no independent exhaustive historical priority review has been performed.

value.rationale: The two observables are canonical complementary summaries of a single viewing plane. Their full joint law supplies structural information missing from both complete marginals: 20 exact cone nestings, forbidden (8,12) and (10,12) pairs, four positive support classes, and a closed-form negative covariance. This natural geometric compatibility theorem is more than a recomputed table or arbitrary slice, and it is a useful benchmark for stochastic geometric section/projection methods.
